expertTake: The DEKOPRO 15-inch leads this guide on the strength of 15 amp copper motor. For the lowest entry cost the BILT HARD 16-inch is the sensible route, with the caveat of less proven brand. Skip these combos if compacted soil is your main problem. A real core aerator pulls plugs that a blade reel cannot.
introParagraphs: Combination machines promise to dethatch, scarify and aerate with one tool. In practice the second reel is a blade or spike reel, which slices or punctures the surface rather than pulling soil cores.
This guide compares electric 2-in-1 machines by which reels ship, how they swap and how well the depth controls work. It is straight about what the aerator language means on a listing.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Tine and blade material decide durability. Stainless or spring steel resists rust better than plain carbon steel, and bent tines should be replaced rather than reused. The BILT HARD 16-inch and the WEN DT1516 both use replaceable tines, so a spare set is cheap insurance. Dull or bent parts tear grass instead of lifting thatch.

Working width runs from 14 inches on the Greenworks 13A 14-inch to 16 inches on the BILT HARD 16-inch. A wider path means fewer passes, but it needs a stronger motor and a larger bag, and it is harder to steer around beds and trees. Under about a quarter acre, the narrower models are often the better handlers. Measure gate clearance, since the machine body can be wider than the path.

Depth control is what prevents scalping. The DEKOPRO 15-inch offers adjustable depth positions, and published ranges run from a small raise above the soil to a few tenths of an inch below it. Start at the shallowest setting on every lawn, because a fixed deep setting shreds healthy roots. Rough, uneven lawns deserve more depth steps.

Power source shapes the whole ownership. Corded models like the DEKOPRO 15-inch run indefinitely but need a heavy-gauge outdoor cord, ideally 14 gauge or thicker, to avoid voltage drop. Cordless machines trade the cord for runtime, so match battery capacity to lawn size. Every pick in this set is corded, which avoids runtime anxiety.

Corded motors are rated in amps and cordless ones in volts and battery capacity. The DEKOPRO 15-inch lists 15 amp copper, 3500 RPM. Higher amperage holds rpm in dense thatch, but a 15 amp tool is already at the limit of a 15 amp household circuit, so it must not share the outlet with anything else. Compare rpm only between machines with the same reel type.

Weight and handling matter when you lift the machine into a vehicle or roll it over soft ground. Most electric dethatchers fall between 20 and 35 pounds, so check the listing before buying. The Westinghouse 16-inch is worth comparing against the DEKOPRO 15-inch for how it feels to handle. Folding handles and a bag that detaches without tools help.

faq.q: How do I know if I need to dethatch?
faq.a: Cut a small plug and measure the spongy brown layer between grass and soil. If it is thicker than about half an inch, dethatching helps; thinner than that, leave it. A machine like the BILT HARD 16-inch is overkill for a thin layer.

faq.q: When is the best time to dethatch?
faq.a: Dethatch when the grass is actively growing, early fall for cool-season grass and late spring for warm-season grass. Soil should be moist but not soaked. Avoid dethatching during drought or dormancy.

Some listings, such as the WEN DT1516, are labeled dethatcher and aerator, but the blade reel only slices thin grooves in the surface. It does not remove soil cores. For true compaction relief, use a core aerator separately.
Yes, and it works best right after scarifying because seed contacts bare soil. Rake up loosened debris with the DEKOPRO 15-inch's bag, spread seed and keep the area moist for a few weeks.

faq.q: Is a cordless dethatcher strong enough?
faq.a: For small to mid-size lawns, yes, if you have enough battery capacity. Heavy thatch drains packs quickly, so plan on a spare. Corded models such as the DEKOPRO 15-inch have no runtime limit.

faq.q: How long an extension cord can I use?
faq.a: Use a heavy-gauge outdoor cord, 14 gauge or thicker for long runs, and keep it as short as practical. A thin cord drops voltage and makes the motor stall. Plug the machine into a circuit that is not shared with other heavy loads.
